profile.headline: Software Engineer at WEX
profile.summary:
Whether it’s someone dealing with a delivery company that keeps delaying their order, someone who gets charged an extra $200 because they clicked the wrong button, or simply someone who can’t figure out how to use an app, I’ve witnessed countless cases of the frustration brought about by poor user experiences. On the other hand, when all the ducks line up in a row, the joy and satisfaction that comes with a great user experience is something I can’t get enough of, from the subtle smiles to the life-changing moments.

So when my interests in problem solving, building, and STEM led me to pursue becoming a software engineer, I figured out pretty quickly that I wanted my focus to be where I could have the greatest effect on the user experience: the front-end. Though I’ve gotten the opportunity to hone my skills across the stack, the front-end is where I find the most fulfillment and feel I’m able to make the most impact. From talking with customers to working side-by-side with product designers, speaking into the experience and making it come to life is where I find my calling.

company.name: Ramsey Solutions, A Dave Ramsey Company

positions.title: Information Technology Intern
positions.description:
Developed scripts and applications to assist the Common Platforms team, whose role is to maintain and improve the systems and services that the other teams in IT rely on.

My main focus during the internship was developing a web application for my team that would display the status of the many different systems and applications that they managed (as well as some of their dependencies) in a way that is quick and easy for them to view. It would also depict how those devices were connected. This would help them more quickly identify the root cause of issues they might be facing.

positions.title: Quality Assurance Intern
positions.description:
Developed automated regression tests for Converge Mobile, a mobile application for businesses to process card payments, 

Most of my time was spent developing these regression tests and making sure they worked as intended, so that when new features were added to the application, the tests would properly identify whether those features negatively impacted any of the features already in place. These tests were created so that they could be run on real devices, as well as on multiple different devices in parallel. This work also allowed me to identify bugs in the application and submit detailed reports so that they could be quickly fixed.
